CANONICAL_NAME.value: E 2.6 -- a superposition-based theorem prover for first-order logic with equality (Stephan Schulz)

VERSION.value: github.com/eprover/eprover master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes; 3.x line)

value.lineage: Automated theorem proving by SATURATION: the resolution lineage (Robinson 1965) as refined into superposition/paramodulation with term orderings and a given-clause loop -- Otter (McCune 1988) -> E (Schulz 1998-) and Vampire, the engines that win CASC. Distinct execution model from every solver in the vault: it searches a space of DERIVED CLAUSES for the empty clause, proving a conjecture by refuting its negation. First theorem-proving fossil.

value.built_to: decide whether a first-order conjecture follows from axioms, by systematically deriving consequences until it finds a contradiction with the negated goal
value.pressure: the search space of derivable clauses is unbounded; term orderings, literal selection and the given-clause loop keep it tractable on real problems
value.success_means: a conjecture that is a theorem is proved (empty clause derived); a checkable proof object is emitted

value.pressure: unbounded search; combinatorial explosion of derived clauses
value.failure_condition: the prover runs forever or exhausts memory on a true theorem it cannot order well (incompleteness of the strategy, not of the calculus)
